quote: Specific eosinophil markers included CLC, MS4A3, CCR3 and the “Th2” cytokines IL4 and IL13 (Supplementary Fig. 3a ), while the HCAR3 , FCGR3B (CD16b), CMTM2 and PROK2 were specific neutrophil markers (Fig. 2b ).
summary: CMTM2 is named among four neutrophil marker genes in single-cell data from inflamed human intestine, with no gene-specific result.

quote: Then, the panel of 109 probe sets was refined in further study to a smaller set of 13 genes signature (CMTM2, C5AR1, FGF2, GK, HGF, L1RN, LILRA2, NAMPT, PAPPA, SNCA, SOD2, STEAP4, ZBED3).
summary: CMTM2 appears only as one member of a 13-gene signature predicting anti-TNF response in UC, cited from earlier work.

quote: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of intestinal lamina propria cells from IBD patients has further confirmed the presence of a neutrophil developmental continuum within the inflamed mucosa, identifying precursor-like subsets expressing high levels of HCAR3 and CMTM2 that are enriched in areas of severe inflammation ( 110 ).
summary: A review on neutrophils in IBD notes that CMTM2-high neutrophil subsets are enriched in severely inflamed mucosa, without new data.

quote: In the set of 20 top tissue-specific genes, the largest numbers of eQTLs in corresponding tissues (tissue samples, n > 350) were found for the following genes: SLURP1 (Skin—Sun Exposed / Skin—Not Sun Exposed, 684/291 eQTLs), CNTF (Nerve—Tibial, 669), CMTM2 (Testis, 58), ADIPOQ (Adipose—Subcutaneous, 45), TNFRSF11B (Thyroid, 40) and CCL11 (Colon—Sigmoid, 39 eQTLs).
summary: CMTM2 is listed among tissue-specific cytokine genes with testis eQTLs in a pan-cytokine GTEx analysis, with nothing specific to UC.

quote: CMTM2, an immune-related gene within the CMTM family, plays a significant role in tumor progression, and prognosis in gastric cancer ( Qian et al., 2020 ).
summary: A review of Sijunzi decoction mentions CMTM2 only in gastric cancer, where the decoction raises its expression; nothing on UC.

quote: Our results revealed that GMFG, GNG11, CLEC4D, CMTM2, VAMP5, S100A8, S100A12 and DGKQ are potential diagnostic biomarkers of AS and UC.
summary: CMTM2 is one of eight shared differentially expressed genes proposed as a diagnostic marker for UC and ankylosing spondylitis by ROC analysis; it was not among those validated by RT-PCR.

quote: The common cell marker are following: plasma cell – DERL3, MZB1, IGHG1; CD4 + T cell–CD4; neutrophils cell – PROK2, CMTM2, CXCL8, FCRG3B, AQP9, S100A8, S100A9; CD8 + T – CD8A, CD8B; fibroblasts cell – LUM, FGF7, ADAMDEC1; macrophages cell – CD68, CD14 C1QA, C1QB; epithelial cell – EPCAM, KRT19, CLDN4; B cell – MS4A1 (CD20), CD19, CD79A, IGHG1, MZB1, SDC1; cycling cells (PC and B cells) – TUBB, TOP2A, MKI67.
summary: CMTM2 is only used as a neutrophil marker in a list of cell-type markers; the UC susceptibility genes identified were ADCY3, ITGB6 and MTMR3.

quote: “AIF1”, “CD14”, “CMTM2”, “FCGR3B”, “LYZ”, “MS4A2” and “TPSAB1” as the marker genes for myeloid cells ( Figure 1B ).
summary: CMTM2 is listed as a myeloid cell marker in a Crohn's disease single-cell analysis; the diagnostic genes were IFITM3, PSMB9 and TAP1.

quote: ROC curves revealed that GMFG, GNG11, CLEC4D, CMTM2, VAMP5, S100A8, S100A12 and DGKQ may serve as diagnostic biomarkers for the individuals with AS and UC.
summary: CMTM2 is one of eight shared differentially expressed genes that ROC analysis suggests could be diagnostic biomarkers for UC and ankylosing spondylitis, using public datasets only.

quote: The top 10 genes positively correlated with APRIL/TNFSF13 expression in the TME included CD4, ITGAM, SLC7A7, LAIR1, ITGB2, SELPLG, TMEM176B, HCK, TMEM176A , and CYTH4 , while the top 10 negatively correlated genes were COA7, WDR43, NCL, PAICS, WDR12, NOLC1, TEX10, EXOSC2, MSANTD3 and CCDC43 .
summary: In a melanoma study, CYTH4 appears only as a gene correlated with APRIL/TNFSF13 expression and immune infiltration; nothing about UC.

quote: At the protein marker level, high expression of ARHGAP43 indicates poor prognosis [ 996 ], while hematopoietic stem cell transplantation can improve outcomes; cytohesin 4 (CYTH4) promotes cell growth through immunomodulation and serves as an independent adverse prognostic factor [ 997 ]; stathmin 1 (STMN1) activates the PI3K/AKT pathway, and its expression level may be linked to survival [ 986 ].
summary: A broad biomarker review mentions CYTH4 as an adverse prognostic factor in a cancer context, with nothing about UC.

quote: By applying a genomics approach and differential expression analysis in CeD intestinal biopsies, we prioritize potential causal genes at these novel loci, including LTBR, CYTH4, and RAC2.
summary: A celiac disease immunochip study prioritises CYTH4 as a candidate causal gene at the 22q13.1 locus; no direction is stated and UC is not studied.

quote: ARHGAP25, CYTH4, ITGB7, APOC1, WDFY4, MARCO and PLCB2 are pivotal genes intimately linked to AS and the UPRmt.
summary: CYTH4 is one of seven hub genes of a mitochondrial stress signature in atherosclerosis; the paper does not study UC.

quote: Thus, inhibition of GLT1D1 activity may be a new therapeutic direction for DLBCL.
summary: A glycosylation review reports that GLT1D1 glycosylates PD-L1 in lymphoma and suggests inhibiting it for DLBCL; nothing on UC.

quote: There was some evidence of association (p < 0.05) for 16 SNVs across 12 genes, CHTOP , A RIH2 , NICN1 , PLSCR1 , IL12B , BTNL2 , QRSL1 , CALML5 , GLT1D1 , RTEL1 , ATG4B and TBX21 ( S5 Table ).
summary: GLT1D1 is one of 12 genes with nominal rare-variant association signals in an IBD sequencing study, with no gene-specific result.

quote: It suggests that GLT1D1 probably is a promising biomarker for lymphoma; further studies on cancer-type–dependent glycosylation pathways are needed.
summary: A review notes GLT1D1 stabilises PD-L1 by N-glycosylation in B-cell lymphoma and may be a lymphoma biomarker; nothing about UC.
LIR6 here is the name used for a tick salivary LTB4-binding lipocalin, not the human LILRA1 receptor.

quote: The intersection of four hub gene lists revealed 25 hub genes: FCGR3A, FGR, MNDA, SELL, NCF2, FYB1, EVI2B, LY86, TREM1, LILRA1, IGSF6, CTSS, CXCR4, LCK, CLEC12A, FCN1, CXCL2, VNN2 P2RY13, LYZ, CCR3, EOMES, MMP7, CD3G and CLEC4E ( Figure 3C ).
summary: LILRA1 appears only in a list of 25 hub genes shared by obesity and periodontitis; the paper does not study UC.

quote: Many of these receptors (LILRA1, LILRB1 and LILRB2) are more hypo-methylated in severe UC than in mild UC ( Table 2 ) [ 18 ].
summary: LILRA1 is one of three leukocyte receptor genes more hypo-methylated in severe than mild UC mucosa, with no gene-specific functional result.

quote: Members of the leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor family include two classes: activating LILRs (LILRA1-6) and inhibitory LILRs (LILRB1-5) [ 15 , 22 ].
summary: This LILRB4 review names LILRA1 only as a member of the activating LILR family.

quote: Furthermore , LILRB1, LILRA1 , and LILRA2 are highly enriched in non-classical monocytes with means of 290.46, 632.40, and 128.35, respectively, compared to the classical monocytes with an average of 87.91, 204.29, and 123.98, respectively.
summary: In an IBD exome and expression analysis, LILRA1 was upregulated and highly expressed in non-classical monocytes; the paper's main variant findings concern LILRB1 and PRSS3.

quote: LILRs consist of two pseudogenes and 11 functional genes encoding five activating (LILRA1, 2, 4–6), five inhibitory (LILRB1–5) and one soluble (LILRA3) form.
summary: LILRA1 is named only as a member of the LILR family in a paper that studies LILRA3 in IBD.

quote: The receptors for HLA-B27 homodimers were found to be KIR3DL1, LILRB2 ( 74 ), KIR3DL2 ( 75 ) and LIR6 ( 68 ) and expressed on lymphocytes, monocytes and Natural Killer Cells (NKs) ( 75 ).
summary: A spondyloarthritis review lists LIR6 (LILRA1) as a receptor for HLA-B27 homodimers; no UC data.

quote: Similarly, F. nucleatum may be also associated with promoted gene expression in HNSCC, including SULF1 , TREM2 , MMP2 , KRTAP5-10 , SCN5A , JAKMIP1 , KRTAP5-9 , ECE2 , LILRA6 , KCNAB2 , ERC2 , KIF26A , USP31 , PLCG2 , and SLC22A25 (log2FC ≥ 0.5, adjusted p ≤ 0.01), given the observed hypomethylation of gene promoters related to the enrichment of F. nucleatum .
summary: LILRA6 is one of 15 genes listed as possibly upregulated with F. nucleatum in head and neck cancer; nothing about UC.

quote: Genes such as CSF1, SPP1, FAM20C, and Cst7 were upregulated and are related to osteoclast formation and inflammation, while genes such as LILRA6, MMP9, and COL18A1, which are downregulated, are involved in bone formation and osteoclast regulation [ 218 ].
summary: A review on Alzheimer's disease and bone health mentions LILRA6 as a downregulated gene tied to bone formation and osteoclast regulation; no UC data.
